name: Epsilon Indi B
type: Pair of brown dwarfs (Ba and Bb, spectral types T1 and T6)
summary: Epsilon Indi B is not one object but two brown dwarfs, Ba and Bb, orbiting each other. Together they travel far from the star Epsilon Indi A, and they are the nearest known pair of brown dwarfs. They are so close together that SPHEREx sees them as a single point of light.
why_interesting: The pair moves quickly across the sky, so you can see it shift between SPHEREx images taken months apart. Its infrared spectrum shows what the atmosphere of a cool brown dwarf looks like.

facts.label: Distance
facts.compare: Measured from its parallax (270.66 milliarcseconds). An older value, measured for the star Epsilon Indi A, gives 11.8 light-years; the small difference does not change anything we show.

facts.label: Proper motion
facts.compare: In half a year it moves more than 2 arcseconds, about a third of a SPHEREx pixel.

facts.label: Mass
facts.compare: Weighed by following their orbit around each other for about 10 years, with an error of less than 1%.

facts.label: Temperature
facts.compare: Less than a quarter as hot as the Sun's surface. Estimated by fitting two families of models to their light.

facts.label: Age
facts.compare: A bit younger than the Sun (4.6 billion years).
